title: decade is an MCP server that relays tool calls to panes
body:
An agent cannot ask decade for anything. ACP has no way for a client to
offer tools to the agent; the agent's tools are its own or come from MCP
servers the client names when it opens a session.

## Proposal

decade itself is the MCP server, over streamable HTTP on a local port, so no
bridge process exists. A tools/call becomes a message on the pane socket to
the pane the tool names, and the pane's reply is the tool result.

The tools come from the panes. A pane's hello grows an optional `tools` list
in MCP's own schema form; decade's tools/list is the union of what the
occupied panes offer, named `<pane>.<verb>`, plus decade's own `focus` and
`panes`. A new pane program adds tools without a change to decade. coax
passes decade's MCP address in the ACP session's server list.

Decided with Jack on 2026-11-06, in place of a bridge beside decade: one
protocol per audience, the socket for programs in panes and MCP for agents,
with decade the only thing that speaks both.

## Rejected

- A separate MCP bridge process forwarding to the socket. Defines every verb
  twice and adds a process for nothing decade cannot do itself.
- MCP everywhere, with each pane program an MCP server. A TUI's stdio is its
  terminal, so each pane would need an HTTP server; the agent would address
  ports instead of roles; and MCP flows host to server, so a pane could not
  tell the chat anything. Most traffic here is not from the agent.
- Markers in the agent's prose that the chat parses. Fragile, visible in
  transcripts, no channel for errors.

## Open

- Which Rust MCP implementation: rmcp, the official SDK, is the first thing
  to check.
- Whether the pane socket's hello carries the tool schemas from the start
  or decade hardcodes the code pane's three verbs first.
